item_verdicts.goal: §15 makes imas-alambic's write fetch the EDDB channels a pulse's signal maps declare before writing it, so a write at the facility (empty cache) fetches rather than refusing. At head d1035fa8: write_pulse builds one ChannelRequest per distinct (category, dname) via _channel_requests and passes them to eddb.fetch_channels before reading, so a cached pulse makes no transport call (fetch_channels returns early when nothing is missing); a refused channel is skipped by _served_entries and carried on a new WriteReceipt.refused field without stopping the write; settings.py resolves eddb_host (flag --eddb-host, variable IMAS_ALAMBIC_EDDB_HOST, then unset) and eddb_remote.extractor_for_host is the single setting-to-transport owner (unset -> ssh jt-60sa, host name -> ssh_command_for_host, local -> empty ssh_command with remote_python=sys.executable); DEFAULT_SSH_COMMAND is ssh_command_for_host("jt-60sa"); imas-alambic config prints eddb_host with its source; install/imasdb.sh exports IMAS_ALAMBIC_EDDB_HOST=local.
item_verdicts.manifest: Read; it records orientation, two commits (c5d959a2, d1035fa8), baseline_suite and after_suite as completed with 0 failures, the negative control EXIT=1 with the two failing ids, and two self-reported follow-ons. Every quoted result I checked reproduces, except the head log's revision stamp and the ruff log, both recorded as findings.

justifications.durability: The behaviour is pinned by committed tests with a firing negative control: test_write_fetch.py asserts one transport call on the first write, none on the overwrite, and a refused channel reported while the served channel is written; test_settings.py pins the precedence, the unset route, the local transport and the launcher export. The blank-string eddb_host branch and the empty-request path are unpinned but both are minor and the empty-request path cannot issue a transport call.
justifications.evidence: The base and head gate logs name revision, tree, module and cwd and reach their pytest summary line with EXIT=0, and the negative control fires with the two new test ids absent from both green arms -- I reproduced all four. Against that, the head arm's log stamps the base revision 7e5e9ca6 rather than the head c5d959a2, so a reader cannot reconcile the log with the head it purportedly measured, and ruff.log on disk is the earlier failing run (EXIT=1, 4 errors) while the manifest's "ruff exit 0" pass has no log; I confirmed the pass independently on the extracted head.
justifications.fit: The change is idiomatic and documented by mechanism docstrings (extractor_for_host, ssh_command_for_host, _channel_requests, _eddb_host); no plan, sprint, ticket or version identifier appears in any source path, symbol or comment, and the commits carry a conventional subject and a body.
justifications.goal_fidelity: Every clause of the §15 done-when is implemented and pinned by a committed test, and each clause independently reproduces: the fetch-then-write, the no-transport-on-second-write, the refused-channel receipt, the eddb_host precedence, the unset jt-60sa route, the local transport with sys.executable, the composed ssh command keeping -F ~/.ssh/config and the module shell, the config line and the launcher export.
justifications.reuse: The change reuses fetch_channels, ChannelRequest/ChannelRefusal, is_cached and the existing RemoteEddbExtractor, and makes extractor_for_host the single owner of the setting-to-transport mapping rather than adding a parallel path; DEFAULT_SSH_COMMAND is derived from ssh_command_for_host instead of a second spelling.
justifications.scope_discipline: git diff --name-only 7e5e9ca6..d1035fa8 lists exactly the nine declared write paths, and the declared figures directory was correctly left unwritten because the done-when names no figure.
